title: What's going on with rpg maker.net?

posts.author: ZENWARECO
posts.body:
Anyone know what's going on with rpgmaker.net?  For whatever reason it's telling me this when I'm trying to get in.
​
Your connection is not private​
Attackers might be trying to steal your information from
rpgmaker.net
(for example, passwords, messages, or credit cards).
Learn more about this warning
net::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID
I don't really rpgmaker.net ever doing this before.  I have no idea what's going on.
Meh??

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
For the past several months, rpgmaker.net has been down to the server host being shut down (or something to that effect). The website doesn't exist at this point in time, but they still have the domain up linking to the
archive.org collection of every game that existed on the site
.
They have been working on remaking the entire website in the meantime. Maybe. Possibly. It's a massive undertaking, whatever it is they decide to do.
When a website has its certificate run out, it just means that they haven't updated it for the domain name in a while. There's a chance that the domain itself could have expired and it was purchased by a malicious actor, but it is more likely that whoever is in charge of maintaining the domain just hasn't renewed the certificate and that's why you get this warning.
Unfortunately, there's not really a reason to visit there at the moment. They have a
Discord server
if you'd like to get updates.

posts.author: RachelTheSeeker
posts.body:
Indeed
@Rhymaestro
, the games should be available on the Internet Archive link that Freedom posted. I was even able to find a game I missed, that the dev had deleted.
Pilgrim's Road
, what a trip. I think it even won an award for RMN's Misaos thing, the year that game was created.
...and now, I've avoided the subject as much as I could, so now let's lean into the "firebrand" part of my user(re-)name. RMN has been struggling with not only keeping their server up for a while now, but AFAIK the main admin had also been pretty quiet.
The Discord server is used much, much more than the site had been for years now. Problem is that its Discord community was pretty toxic. A lot of jerks hanging around the General and Memes channels, some of which don't even make games for the game jam events. And much less actual, full-length games. The ones who actually made non-jam games on RMN rarely if ever hung out on the Discord server. That says something.
Let's just say I heavily respect this forum's no-politics, no-swearing rule. The moderators giving a lot of slaps on the wrist at best to the freeloaders, while punishing people who snapped at their nonsense. Reminds me of the kind of nonsense from grade school, where the bullies were ignored and the kids who did something about it got in trouble. So overall? Bunch of maladjusted 20-somethings pretty much getting off scot-free for being terminally online jerks, and not bothering to do what the the site and Discord server was meant for: discuss and work on RPG Maker games.
And I say that as a former maladjusted 20-something that hung out there for years. It's the opposite of "steel sharpens steel", or something. I'm not even saying that other non-RM channels were a problem. I just don't like the people there, and the ones who put the least effort into RM stuff were probably the most outspoken jerks.
Am I biased from my own experiences, and probably have a grudge that taints those biases? Totally. No doubt. 100%. And I'm definitely guilty of having lashed out there on multiple occasions. Like I said: I didn't like most of the regulars there by the time I left (and a week-long ban certainly put things into perspective). I just didn't fit in to their specific clique, to describe my feelings against them nicely. And as usual, I tend to be part of the problem. So I'm not innocent by any means.
Look. I am grateful for the backups of the games hosted there, because there were so many. A lot of RPG Maker stuff has been lost over the years (looking at you, XP and VX scripts), and the armchair archivist in me is saddened by that fact. And I had a lot of fun there with the community too, in my better years on RMN.
But personally? Given the rot and mismanagement of the site and its Discord server, it had it coming. Good riddance.
But what do I know? Find out if you fit in there or not, yourself. I just felt like ranting on something that's been on my mind for a couple years now. Like, the reason I stopped RPG Making to begin with in 2022.

, and Steam, but they all look abandoned. This is a rather unusual list using
Wayback Machine

They should use an open redundant system (clone/mirror/repository) if the developers allow it and that would increase the system performance.

ZENWARECO
's Mysterious Aeges and Diabolical Vengeance. So, while writing this, the servers mysteriously came back up. This is the only reference I could find.
https://web.archive.org/web/20240304093935/https://rpgmaker.net/games/12800/
I am unsure what happened to the game. Maybe try again later, the servers could have collapsed so he moved as much over as he could? You would have to ask him.

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body: RMN has been really slow for a long time. Years. I don't think it has felt snappy since like 2014. I'm pretty confident they aren't being hit by a cyber attack. The server is just too slow and perhaps has reliability issues. I got it to load and then tried again and got the "system is down" screen.
